observations: The inputs are the forehead and hen, and two designated referents bear the corresponding descriptions.
Padamañjarī preserves transparent conventional association. Bāla requires inherited rūḍhi as opposed to merely stipulating a new name.
The mendicant's restricted forward glance uses the idea of a hen's short landing range independently of an actual bird landing.
Amara spells the incapacity-of-attendant lemma with short initial a. Bāla quotes the description with the graded stem.
Amara additionally makes kaukkuṭika a lexical description for hypocrisy.
The customary justification is dharmya from the separate ablative yat construction. The outer relation here is genitive.
Four identical institutional stems take their customary sense with neuter case in Kāśikā.
Padamañjarī supplies the separate dauvārika example and describes the insertion process.
Kāśikā lists ten gaṇa inputs and displays the first two forms. The University text also displays yājamānam.
Potṛ and udgātṛ are direct regular examples, and yātṛ has a worked example in the University text.
Padamañjarī treats ritual hotṛ as gaṇa-owned and preserves both the corrected example and reported action-word interpretation.
Nṛ and nara have separately stated support, with a shared feminine outcome.
Viśasitṛ loses the explicitly owned iṭ while its prefix and ṛ-final agent frame continue.
Vibhājayitṛ loses ṇic and retains iṭ. The distributive causative has separately retained root grade.
Padamañjarī's customs exaction is assessed per consignment load and can be a means for the owner to reclaim the same goods.
Śaulkaśālika with initial ś is given in the fuller witness. The rival display omits that initial letter. Kāśikā detaches levies from the requirement of customary justification.
decisions: Admit the specific two seeing-based designations and source-exclude ordinary looking at a forehead or a hen as sufficient evidence.
Preserve the conventional-denotation and rūḍhi formulations separately. They support the same selected cases with ṭhak.
Admit Amara's exact short nominative as an attestation in the attendant sense. Leave its independent morphological route and other cases Open.
Admit the independently defined Amara hypocrisy stem without extending the Pāṇinian named mendicant cut.
Admit the four Kāśikā neuter fibres and Padamañjarī's separate door-associated customary form.
Admit the ten named members, with formal derivation credit and separately marked examples.
Use the ṛ-final añ gate for potṛ, udgātṛ and yātṛ. On the corrected Padamañjarī reading potṛ replaces the divergent hotṛ example.
Keep ritual hotṛ in its gaṇa, and action hotṛ in the secondary reported añ history. Mark the action history as source-conditional.
Preserve regular nṛ and explicit local nṛ/nara support with a single shared feminine set of forms.
Delete the viśasitṛ iṭ under the local vārttika; keep vi and its grade.
Delete vibhājayitṛ’s ṇic layer and preserve the causative root grade and tṛc's iṭ.
Admit the standalone levy context and the positive enforced-payment example. Retain the paleographic discrepancy Open with positive evidence for initial ś.
Preserve the two different syntactic families and their distinct genders even when the stem is shared. The separate appointment rule retains its locative input.
